questions.question: Which two numbers and which two signs should be interchanged to balance the following equation? 24 ÷ 16 - 96 + 48 × 12 = 195
questions.questionHtml:
Which two numbers and which two signs should be interchanged to balance the following equation?

24 ÷ 16 - 96 + 48 × 12 = 195
questions.solution:
According to the BODMAS rule:

Option 1 : 24 and 48, × and ÷

Given:

24 ÷ 16 - 96 + 48 × 12 = 195

After interchange the numbers and signs;

48 × 16 - 96 + 24 ÷ 12 = 195

By BODMAS rule

48 × 16 - 96 + 2 = 195

768 - 96 + 2 = 195

770 – 96 = 195

674 = 195 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 2 : 24 and 16, - and ÷

Given: 

24 ÷ 16 - 96 + 48 × 12 = 195

After interchange the numbers and signs;

16 - 24 ÷ 96 + 48 × 12 = 195

By BODMAS rule

16 – 0.25 + 48 × 12 = 195

16 – 0.25 + 576 = 195

592 – 0.25 = 195

591.75 = 195 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 3: 12 and 16, × and ÷

Given:

24 ÷ 16 - 96 + 48 × 12 = 195

After interchange the numbers and signs;

24 × 12 - 96 + 48 ÷ 16 = 195

By BODMAS rule

24 × 12 - 96 + 3 = 195

288 – 96 + 3 = 195

291 – 96 = 195

195 = 195 (LHS = RHS)

Option 4: 12 and 48, × and +

Given:

24 ÷ 16 - 96 + 48 × 12 = 195

After interchange the numbers and signs;

24 ÷ 16 - 96 × 12 + 48 = 195

By BODMAS rule

1.5 – 96 × 12 + 48 = 195

1.5 – 1152 + 48 = 195

49.5 – 1152 = 195

- 1102.5 = 195 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Hence, the answer is “12 and 16, × and ÷”.

384 ÷ 16 - 72 + 9 × 10 = 2
questions.solution:
According to the BODMAS rule:

Option 1 : 6 and 9

Given:

384 ÷ 16 - 72 + 9 × 10 = 2

After interchanging the digits;

384 ÷ 19 - 72 + 6 × 10 = 2

By BODMAS rule

20.21 - 72 + 6 × 10 = 2

20.21 - 72 + 60 = 2

80.21 – 72 = 2

8.21 = 2 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 2 : 4 and 8

Given:

384 ÷ 16 - 72 + 9 × 10 = 2

After interchanging the digits;

348 ÷ 16 - 72 + 9 × 10 = 2

By BODMAS rule

21.75 - 72 + 9 × 10 = 2

21.75 - 72 + 90 = 2

111.75 - 72 = 2

39.75 = 2 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 3: 3 and 7

Given:

384 ÷ 16 - 72 + 9 × 10 = 2

After interchanging the digits;

784 ÷ 16 - 32 + 9 × 10 = 2

By BODMAS rule

49 - 32 + 9 × 10 = 2

49 - 32 + 90 = 2

139 - 32 = 2

107 = 2 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 4: 7 and 9

Given:

384 ÷ 16 - 72 + 9 × 10 = 2

After interchanging the digits;

384 ÷ 16 - 92 + 7 × 10 = 2

By BODMAS rule

24 - 92 + 7 × 10 = 2

24 – 92 + 70 = 2

94 – 92 = 2

2 = 2 (LHS = RHS)

Hence, the correct answer is “7 and 9”.

questions.question: The process of wastewater treatment is commonly called ______ treatment.
questions.questionHtml: The process of wastewater treatment is commonly called ______ treatment.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is sewage.

Key Points

  • The process of wastewater treatment is commonly called sewage treatment.
  • Cleaning of water is a process of removing pollutants before it enters a water body or is reused.
  • There are mainly three types of sewage treatment stages primary, secondary or biological, and tertiary sewage treatments.

Additional Information

  • Primary treatment (Physical process):
    • It is the process of physically removing small and large particles from sewage.
    • The floating debris is first removed by filtration through wire mesh screens in a sequential filtration.
  • Secondary or biological sewage treatment:
    • It is the removal of biodegradable organic matter from sewage or similar types of wastewater.
    • This is usually done with the help of microorganisms, hence it is called biological treatment.
  • Tertiary treatment (Chemical process):
    • Biological treatment precedes chemical treatment in the treatment process.
    • Chemical treatment is now considered as a tertiary treatment that can be more broadly defined as “treatment of wastewater by a process involving chemical treatment”.

questions.question: The 'Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan' (PM-AASHA) has________ components to rationalise the government agricultural produce price and policy for efficiency, savings by way of reduction of wastages and leakages in storage and make fiscal gains.
questions.questionHtml: The 'Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan' (PM-AASHA) has________ components to rationalise the government agricultural produce price and policy for efficiency, savings by way of reduction of wastages and leakages in storage and make fiscal gains.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is three.

Key Points

  • The 'Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan' (PM-AASHA) has three components to rationalise the government agricultural produce price and policy for efficiency, savings by way of reduction of wastages and leakages in storage and making fiscal gains.
  • It is a scheme that guarantees a Minimum support price (MSP) to the farmers.
  • The scheme is an effort of the government’s commitment to ensure remunerative prices to farmers for their produce as announced in the Union Budget for 2018. 

Additional Information

  • The scheme comprises three sub-schemes:
    • Price Support Scheme (PSS)
      • ​Under this, physical procurement of pulses, oilseeds, and Copra is to be done by Central Nodal Agencies in collaboration with state governments.
    • Price Deficiency Payment Scheme (PDPS)
      • ​This is based on the recommendations of NITI Aayog which suggested “Price Deficiency Payment” for implementation of MSP in crops where procurement is poor.
      • Direct payment of the difference between the MSP and the selling price will be made to pre-registered farmers selling their produce in the notified market yard and thus it does not involve any physical procurement.
    • The pilot of the Private Procurement & Stockist Scheme (PPPS)
      • Under this scheme, participation of the private sector in procurement operations will be piloted.
      • States have the option to roll out the scheme on a pilot basis in selected districts/APMCs involving private stockists.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Notochord is present.

Key Points 

  • Characteristics of Chordates Are:
    • Presence of Notochord: 
      • In the embryonic stage of chordate animals, there is a solid stick-like structure (Just below the central nervous system and above the alimentary canal), this is called the notochord.
    • Presence of dorsal tubular nerve cord: 
      • In chordates, the nervous system is present at the dorsal surface of the body. The nerve cord is the hollow, tubular structure present just below the body wall and above the notochord.
    • Presence of pharyngeal gill clefts: 
      • In every chordate, there is a presence of a pair of lateral gill clefts in the wall of the pharynx for respiration.
      • These may be present in any stage of its life span like in higher chordates gill clefts are present only in the embryonic stage not in adults.
    • Post anal tail:
      • It is the post-anal part of the body.
      • The tail is reduced or absent in many adult chordates.

questions.question: A pole 23 m long reaches a window which is 3 \(\sqrt5\) m above the ground on one side of a street. Keeping its foot at the same point, the pole is turned to the other side of the street to reach a window 4 \(\sqrt15\) m high. What is the width (in m) of the street?
questions.questionHtml: A pole 23 m long reaches a window which is 3\(\sqrt5\) m above the ground on one side of a street. Keeping its foot at the same point, the pole is turned to the other side of the street to reach a window 4\(\sqrt15\) m high. What is the width (in m) of the street?
questions.solution:
Given:

The length of the pole = 23 m

The first window is 3√5 m above the ground and the second window is 4√15 m above the ground.

Formula used:

In a right-angled triangle,

Base = √(Hypotenuse2 - Perpendicular2)

Calculation:

Here, the width of the street = BC

In ΔABO,

BO = √(AO2 - AB2)

= √(232 - 3√52)

= √(529 - 45)

= √484

= 22 m

In ΔOCD,

CO = √(DO2 - DC2)

= √(232 - 4√152)

= √(529 - 240)

= √289 = 17 m

Then, BC = BO + CO

= 22 + 17

= 39 m

∴ The width (in m) of the street is 39 m

questions.question: The width of the path around a square field is 4.5 m and its area is 105.75 m 2 . Find the cost of fencing the field at the rate of Rs. 100 per meter.
questions.questionHtml: The width of the path around a square field is 4.5 m and its area is 105.75 m<sup>2</sup>. Find the cost of fencing the field at the rate of Rs. 100 per meter.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Area of outer path around a square = 4w(s + w), where w = width and s = side of field.

105.75 = 4 × 4.5 × (s + 4.5)

105.75 = 18 × (s + 4.5) ⇒ s + 4.5 = 5.875 ⇒ s = 1.375 m

Perimeter = 4s = 4 × 1.375 = 5.5 m

Cost = 5.5 × 100 = Rs. 550

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 550.

Alternate Method

Given: Width of path (w) = 4.5 m, Area of path = 105.75 m2, Rate = Rs. 100/m.

Formula Used: Area of path = (s + 2w)2 − s2; Cost = Perimeter × Rate

⇒ Let the side of the square field be s.

⇒ Area of path = (s + 2 × 4.5)2 − s2

⇒ 105.75 = (s + 9)2 − s2

⇒ 105.75 = s2 + 81 + 18s − s2

⇒ 105.75 − 81 = 18s

⇒ 24.75 = 18s

⇒ s = 24.75 ÷ 18 = 1.375 m

⇒ Perimeter of the field = 4 × s = 4 × 1.375 = 5.5 m

⇒ Total Cost of fencing = 5.5 × 100 = Rs. 550

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 550.

Additional Information

Area of Path (Outer)

For a square of side 's' and path width 'w' outside: Area = 4w(s + w).

Area of Path (Inner)

For a square of side 's' and path width 'w' inside: Area = 4w(s − w).

Fencing Cost

Total Cost = Perimeter of the region to be fenced × Rate per unit length.

questions.question: Simplify the following expression: \({{{(a^2-4b^2)}^3} + 64 {{(b^2 - 4c^2)}^3} + {{(16c^2 -a^2})^3}} \over {{(a-2b)^3} +{(2b-4c)^3} +{(4c-a)^3}}\)
questions.questionHtml:
Simplify the following expression:

\({{{(a^2-4b^2)}^3} + 64 {{(b^2 - 4c^2)}^3} + {{(16c^2 -a^2})^3}} \over {{(a-2b)^3} +{(2b-4c)^3} +{(4c-a)^3}}\)
questions.solution:
Given:

The given expression = \({{{(a^2-4b^2)}^3} + 64 {{(b^2 - 4c^2)}^3} + {{(16c^2 -a^2})^3}} \over {{(a-2b)^3} +{(2b-4c)^3} +{(4c-a)^3}}\)

Formula used:

If a + b + c = 0 then a3 + b3 + c3 = 3abc

Calculation:

\({{{(a^2-4b^2)}^3} + 64 {{(b^2 - 4c^2)}^3} + {{(16c^2 -a^2})^3}} \over {{(a-2b)^3} +{(2b-4c)^3} +{(4c-a)^3}}\)

= \({{{(a^2-4b^2)}^3} + {{(4b^2 - 16c^2)}^3} + {{(16c^2 -a^2})^3}} \over {{(a-2b)^3} +{(2b-4c)^3} +{(4c-a)^3}}\)

Let, a2 - 4b2 = x; 4b2 - 16c2 = y; 16c2 - a2 = z

Here, x + y + z = a2 - 4b2 + 4b2 - 16c2 + 16c2 - a2 = 0

Then, (a2 - 4b2)3 + (4b2 - 16c2)3 + (16c2 - a2)3 = 3 (a2 - 4b2) (4b2 - 16c2) (16c2 - a2)

Let, a - 2b = p; 2b - 4c = q; 4c - a = r

Here, p + q + r = a - 2b + 2b - 4c + 4c - a = 0

Then, (a - 2b)3 + (2b - 4c)3 + (4c - a)3 = 3 (a - 2b) (2b - 4c) (4c - a)

Now, \({{{(a^2-4b^2)}^3} + {{(4b^2 - 16c^2)}^3} + {{(16c^2 -a^2})^3}} \over {{(a-2b)^3} +{(2b-4c)^3} +{(4c-a)^3}}\) = \(\frac{3(a^2-4b^2)(4b^2-16c^2)(16c^2-a^2)}{3(a-2b)(2b-4c)(4c-a)}\)

= \(\frac{(a+2b)(a-2b)(2b+4c)(2b-4c)(4c+a)(4c-a)}{(a-2b)(2b-4c)(4c-a)}\)  [Using a2 - b2 = (a + b) (a - b) formula]

= (a + 2b) (2b + 4c) (4c + a)

= 2 (a + 2b) (b + 2c) (4c + a)

∴ The value of the expression is 2 (a+ 2b) (b + 2c) (4c + a)

Alternate Method \({{{(a^2-4b^2)}^3} + 64 {{(b^2 - 4c^2)}^3} + {{(16c^2 -a^2})^3}} \over {{(a-2b)^3} +{(2b-4c)^3} +{(4c-a)^3}}\) 

We know that a + b + c = 0 then a3 + b3 + c3 = 3abc

First, we satisfy the numerator and denominator with this equation.

⇒ (a2 - 4b2) + (4b2 - 16c2) + (16c2 - a2) = 0

Now, (a - 2b) + (2b - 4c) + (4c - a) = 0

\({{{(a^2-4b^2)}^3} + 64 {{(b^2 - 4c^2)}^3} + {{(16c^2 -a^2})^3}} \over {{(a-2b)^3} +{(2b-4c)^3} +{(4c-a)^3}}\)

⇒ \({3{(a^2-4b^2)}{(4b^2 - 16c^2)}{(16c^2 -a^2})} \over {3{(a-2b)}{(2b-4c)}{(4c-a)}}\) = \({(a-2b)(a+2b)(2b-4c)(2b+4c)(4c-a)(4c+a)}\over{(a-2b)(2b-4c)(4c-a)}\) 

⇒ (a + 2b){2(b + 2c)}(4c + a)

⇒ 2(a + 2b)(b + 2c)(4c + a)

∴ The value of the expression is 2(a + 2b)(b + 2c)(4c + a).

questions.question: The profit earned by selling an article for Rs. 832 is equal to the loss incurred when the article is sold for Rs. 448. What will be the selling price of the article if it is sold at a 10% loss?
questions.questionHtml: The profit earned by selling an article for Rs. 832 is equal to the loss incurred when the article is sold for Rs. 448. What will be the selling price of the article if it is sold at a 10% loss?
questions.solution:
Given:

The selling price at profit = Rs. 832

The selling price at loss = Rs. 448

Required loss = 10%

Formula used:

S.P. = (100 - Loss%)/100 × C.P.

Where, C.P. = Cost price; S.P. = Selling price

Calculation:

Let, the profit = loss = x

So, 448 + x = 832 - x

⇒ x + x = 832 - 448

⇒ 2x = 384

⇒ x = 384/2 = 192

∴ The cost price = (448 + 192) = (832 - 192) = Rs. 640

So the selling price = (100 - 10)/100 × 640 = Rs. 576

∴ The selling price of the article will be Rs. 576

questions.question: X, Y and Z can do a piece of work in 46 days, 92 days and 23 days, respectively, X started the work. Y joined him after 2 days. If Z joined them after 8 days from the beginning then for how many days did X work?
questions.questionHtml: X, Y and Z can do a piece of work in 46 days, 92 days and 23 days, respectively, X started the work. Y joined him after 2 days. If Z joined them after 8 days from the beginning then for how many days did X work?
questions.solution:
Total work = 92 units (LCM of 46, 92, and 23)

Total efficiency = 2 + 1 + 4 = 7 units

X complete in 2 days = 2 × 2 = 4 work

X and Y complete in 6 days = 6 × (2 + 1) = 18 work

The remaining work = 92 - (4 + 18) = 92 - 22 = 70 work

Time is taken by X, Y, and Z to complete remaining work = 70/7 = 10 days

Total work done by X = 8 + 10 = 18 days

questions.question: How many numbers are there from 500 to 650 (including both) which are divisible neither by 3 nor by 7?
questions.questionHtml: How many numbers are there from 500 to 650 (including both) which are divisible neither by 3 nor by 7?
questions.solution:
The total numbers up to 500 are divisible by 3 = 500/3 → 166 (Quotient)

The total numbers up to 500 are divisible by 7 = 500/7 → 71 (Quotient)

The total numbers up to 500 are divisible by 21 = 500/21 → 23 (Quotient)

The total numbers up to 650 are divisible by 3 = 650/3 → 216 (Quotient)

The total numbers up to 650 are divisible by 7 = 650/7 → 92 (Quotient)

The total numbers up to 650 are divisible by 21 = 650/21 → 30 (Quotient)

⇒ The total number divisible by 3 between 500 and 650 = 216 - 166 = 50

⇒ The total number divisible by 7 between 500 and 650 = 92 - 71 = 21

⇒ The total number divisible by 21 between 500 and 650 = 30 - 23 = 7

The total numbers from 500 to 650 = 150 + 1 = 151

Now, the required numbers = 151 - (50 + 21 - 7) = 151 - 64 = 87

questions.question: The length and the breadth of a rectangle are made to increase and decrease, respectively, by 8% and 10%. What is the percentage increase or decrease in its area?
questions.questionHtml: The length and the breadth of a rectangle are made to increase and decrease, respectively, by 8% and 10%. What is the percentage increase or decrease in its area?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Length = 8% increase (108/100 = 27/25)

Breadth = 10% decrease (90/100 = 9/10)

Area of a rectangle = Length × Breadth

The decrease = 250 - 243 = 7

The decrease percentage = (7/250) × 100 = 2.8%

∴ The percentage of decrease in area is 2.8%

Alternate Method

Given:

The length of the rectangle increased = 8%

The breadth of the rectangle decreased = 10%

Formula used:

Area of a rectangle = Length × Breadth

Calculation:

Let, the length of the rectangle = x

The breadth of the rectangle = y

So, the initial area of the rectangle = xy

The final area of the rectangle = (108x/100) × (90y/100) = 243xy/250

The decrease in area = xy - (243xy/250) = 7xy/250

The percentage = [(7xy/250)/xy] × 100 %

= (7/250) × 100 %

= 14/5 %

= 2.8%

∴ The percentage of decrease in area is 2.8%

Alternate Method Use successive increment and decrements method

Total change = A + B + A × B/100

Where, A and B are successive increments and decrements 

So, total percentage increment and decrements = 8 - 10 - 8 × 10/100 = - 2.8%

( ∵ " - " sign denotes the decrement)

∴ The percentage of decrease in area is 2.8%

questions.solution:
Given:

Formula used:

a3 + b3 = (a + b) (a2 + b2 - ab)

(a + b)2 + (a - b)2 = 2 (a2 + b2)

a2 - b2 = (a + b) (a - b)

Calculation:

(4x + 2y)3 + (4x - 2y)3 = (4x + 2y + 4x - 2y) [(4x + 2y)2 + (4x - 2y)2 - (4x + 2y) (4x - 2y)]

(4x + 2y)3 + (4x - 2y)3 = 8x [2 (16x2 + 4y2)] - (16x2 - 4y2)

(4x + 2y)3 + (4x - 2y)3 = 8x (32x2 + 8y2 - 16x2 + 4y2)

(4x + 2y)3 + (4x - 2y)3 = 8x (16x2 + 12y2)

(4x + 2y)3 + (4x - 2y)3 = 16 (8x3 + 6xy2)   .....(2)

Justifying equations (1) and (2),

A = 8 and B = 6

So, (1/2) √(A2 + B2) = (1/2) √(82 + 62)

= 1/2 × √(64 + 36)

= 1/2 × √100

= 1/2 × 10 = 5

∴ The value of (1/2) √(A2 + B2) is 5

Alternate Method

(4x + 2y)3 + (4x - 2y)3 = 16 (Ax3 + Bxy2) –––––––– (1)

(a +b)3 = a3 + b3 + 3ab(a + b) 

(4x + 2y)3 = 64x3 + 8y3 + 24xy(4x + 2y)

⇒ 64x3 + 8y3 + 96x2y + 48xy2 –––––––– (2)

And, (4x – 2y)3 = 64x3 – 8y3 – 24xy(4x – 2y)

⇒ 64x3 – 8y3 – 96x2y + 48xy2  –––––––– (3)

Adding the equation 1 and 2, we have

 (4x + 2y)3 + (4x - 2y)3 = 128x3 + 96xy2 = 16(8x3 + 6xy2) –– (4)

Justifying equations (1) and (4), we have

A = 8, and B = 6

\({1\over 2 }{(√{A^2 +B^2})}\) = \(1\over2\) \(\sqrt{A^2+B^2}\) = \(1\over2\) \(\sqrt{8^2+6^2}\) 

⇒ \(1\over2\) × 10 = 5

∴ The value of \(1\over2\)\(\sqrt{A^2+B^2}\) is 5
